claims.text: High-energy ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering, combined with controlled oxygen or nitrogen doping, promotes in-situ formation of coherent nanoscale ordered interstitial complexes in refractory HEAs.
The proposed processing route produces a refined-grain microstructure.
The ordered interstitial complexes will be uniformly dispersed and coherent with the matrix.
Ordered interstitial complexes impede dislocation motion.
Ordered interstitial complexes permit controlled stress relaxation.
Powder-processing-induced grain refinement provides grain-boundary strengthening.
Combining powder metallurgy with interstitial doping increases yield strength relative to an as-cast baseline.
The proposed intervention maintains or improves tensile ductility relative to the as-cast baseline.
The proposed intervention modestly increases Young's modulus.
Ordered interstitial complexes enhance energy dissipation near crack tips and thereby improve fracture resistance.
Yield strength and fracture resistance will increase by at least 20–50% relative to the as-cast baseline.
The strategy is most applicable to stable, single-phase BCC HEAs.
Sintering must be hot enough to enable interstitial ordering but cool enough to limit grain growth.
Interstitial concentration has an optimum above which embrittlement or excessive phase separation can occur.
The effect may fail in multiphase HEAs that do not support coherent interstitial ordering.
The strategy may be less effective in inherently brittle alloys or alloys with unsuitable lattice structures.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and predicted outcome require improved ductility, whereas the falsification rule accepts unchanged ductility as success.
The hypothesis and predicted outcome require an increase in Young's modulus, whereas the falsification rule accepts no decrease in modulus.
